data.name: South Korea
data.summary: South Korea taxes residents on worldwide income. Gains on foreign shares cost 22%, while Korean listed shares are exempt below major-shareholder thresholds. Financial income above KRW 20 million a year is taxed at up to 49.5%. Foreigners resident five years or less in ten are taxed on foreign dividends only if they are remitted to Korea. Inheritance tax is estate-based at 10%-50%, with a KRW 500 million deduction, and covers worldwide assets of a resident. There is no net wealth tax, but a national holding tax on high-value housing applies. An exit tax reaches foreign shares from 2027.

regimes.name: Korean resident (worldwide)
regimes.description: Worldwide taxation: foreign-share gains 22%, financial income above KRW 20 million at up to 49.5%; estate-basis inheritance tax up to 50%.
regimes.eligibility: Resident if domiciled in Korea or residing 183 days or more in a tax year (from 2026 also 183 consecutive days spanning two years). Foreigners are taxed worldwide once resident more than five of the last ten years.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains are taxed separately from global income. Gains on Korean listed shares are exempt for shareholders below the 'major shareholder' thresholds (1% stake on KOSPI, or KRW 5 billion market value). Gains on foreign shares are taxed at 20% national plus 10% local income tax (22% in total) after a KRW 2.5 million annual deduction. Major shareholders' Korean shares and unlisted shares are taxed at 22% up to KRW 300 million of gain and 27.5% above (local tax included). Real estate gains are taxed at the progressive rates of 6%-45% plus local tax, with a long-term holding deduction.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: KRW 2.5 million basic deduction per category per year. One house per household exempt under conditions (high-value homes partly taxable).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: The planned financial investment income tax was repealed before taking effect (general knowledge). Exit tax: residents of 5+ years who are major shareholders pay tax on unrealised gains on Korean shares when emigrating; from 1 January 2027 foreign shares are included (above KRW 500 million in total, with carve-outs for foreign employees). Heavier rates for multi-home owners in regulated areas have been suspended by decree (status after May 2026 not verified).

open_questions: Whether short-term foreign residents (5 years or less in the last 10) are taxed on foreign-share gains only when remitted was not confirmed; the special regime therefore keeps 22% on foreign-share gains.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Foreign listed shares 20% + 10% local = 22%. Domestic listed 0 for a holding below 1% and KRW 5 billion. Private business (unlisted, major shareholder) 25% + local = 27.5% on gains above KRW 300 million. Real estate: top 45% + local = 49.5% before the long-term holding deduction (up to 30% of the gain for general property held 15 years; more for a qualifying single home). Foreign real estate taxed the same way once resident 5 years.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Trading as a business is business income at global rates up to 49.5%.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: Major-shareholder shares held under one year: 33%. Real estate held under 1-2 years: higher flat rates (not detailed).
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Gains on foreign assets other than shares are taxable only if the seller has been resident 5 years or more at the time of sale (PwC). Foreign-share gains taxed at 22%.

dividends.summary: Dividends are part of financial income: up to KRW 20 million a year is taxed at 15.4% (14% plus local tax) by withholding; above that, financial income is added to global income at progressive rates up to 45% plus 10% local tax (49.5%). Domestic dividends get a gross-up and dividend tax credit. Foreign dividends of residents taxed on worldwide income are included at global rates with a foreign tax credit. From 2026 to 2028, dividends from qualifying high-dividend Korean companies can be taxed separately at 14%-30%.
dividends.important_exceptions: Foreign residents with five years or less of residence in the last ten are taxed on foreign dividends only if paid by a Korean entity or remitted to Korea (special regime).

open_questions: Dividend gross-up rate for 2026 (10% assumed) not verified.
dividends.rate_basis: Foreign: 45% + 10% local = 49.5% before credit. Domestic: grossed-up dividend (assumed 10% gross-up) taxed at 45% less a credit equal to the gross-up gives 39.5% national + 3.95% local = 43.45% (gross-up rate not verified); qualifying high-dividend companies 2026-2028: separate 14%-30% national.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 22% WHT (20% + local) on dividends to non-residents, reducible by treaty (not opened).
dividends.treaty_network: 97 income tax treaties as of January 2026, including the US and EU states (PwC).
dividends.holding_company_notes: CIT 10%-25% plus local tax; dividends received deduction for Korean subsidiaries (not researched).

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth tax (PwC). Korea does levy a national comprehensive real estate holding tax (CRET, 종합부동산세) on individuals whose total official value of housing exceeds KRW 900 million (KRW 1.2 billion for a one-house household); it is treated here as a property tax, not a wealth tax, because it reaches only Korean real estate and its current rate schedule could not be verified.

종합부동산세 (Comprehensive real estate holding tax)

open_questions: CRET is arguably a limited wealth tax on Korean housing; it was not modelled because the 2026 brackets were not verified.
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Local property tax 0.07%-5% of statutory value (PwC). CRET (national): on (official housing value - KRW 900 million / 1.2 billion) x fair-market-value ratio, progressive rates (top 2.7% for owners of two homes or fewer and up to 5% for three or more under the 2023 law, from general knowledge, not verified), plus 20% rural special tax. A EUR 5 million home would pay CRET. Acquisition tax 1%-12%.

inheritance.summary: Korea levies inheritance tax on the whole estate (estate basis) at 10%-50%: 10% up to KRW 100 million, 20% to 500 million, 30% to 1 billion, 40% to 3 billion and 50% above. A lump-sum deduction of KRW 500 million (or a basic deduction plus personal deductions) and a spouse deduction of at least KRW 500 million (up to 3 billion) apply. Gift tax uses the same rates per recipient, with a deduction for gifts from parents to an adult child of KRW 50 million per 10 years (KRW 20 million for a minor). Gifts within 10 years before death are added back to the estate.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Lump-sum deduction KRW 500 million per estate; spouse deduction KRW 0.5-3 billion; financial asset deduction up to KRW 200 million; 3% credit for timely filing (general knowledge, not verified).
inheritance.important_exceptions: Government reform proposals (heir-based taxation from 2028, higher child deductions, top rate cut) were not in force for 2026 as far as checked; PwC still shows 10%-50%. Business succession deduction for family businesses does not cover a listed portfolio.

inheritance.spouse_note: No exemption: a spouse allowance of at least KRW 500 million and at most KRW 3 billion is deducted (Inheritance and Gift Tax Act art. 19; EY 2026), and the rest of what the spouse inherits is taxed on the 10%-50% scale.
inheritance.gift_tax: Gift tax 10%-50% on each recipient's gifts (10-year aggregation per donor group); KRW 50 million deduction per 10 years for an adult child from lineal ascendants (KRW 20 million for minors); a separate marriage/childbirth gift deduction was added in 2024 (not verified).
inheritance.business_relief: Family business succession deduction (up to KRW 60 billion) for qualifying SMEs and mid-sized companies; not for portfolio shares.
inheritance.foreign_assets: If the deceased was a Korean resident (domicile or residence of 183 days or more), worldwide assets are taxed; for a non-resident deceased, Korean assets only.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Residence of the deceased decides scope; there is no special exclusion for foreign nationals (not verified). Gift tax: a resident recipient is taxed on worldwide gifts.

income.name: South Korea

income_tax.summary: Progressive income tax of 6% to 45% plus local income tax of 10% of the tax gives a top combined marginal rate of 49.5%. Foreign employees who start work in Korea by 31 December 2026 can elect a flat 19% (20.9% with local tax) for up to 20 years in place of progressive rates and deductions; a 21% rate and 2029 deadline are only proposed. Employees pay about 9.7% in pension, health, long-term care and employment insurance.

employment_deduction.note: Earned income deduction: 70% of pay to KRW 5M; 40% of the excess to 15M; 15% to 45M; 5% to 100M; 2% above; capped at KRW 20M.

income_tax.self_employed_notes: Self-employed people are 'local subscribers': they pay the full National Pension (9.5% total rate in 2026, no employer share; PwC) and regional health insurance. The NHIS page gives a 2026 health insurance rate of 7.19%, and long-term care is 13.14% of the health premium (braindetox.kr), which matches PwC's roughly 8.135% for health plus long-term care. The 17.63% used (9.5% + 7.19% x 1.1314) is therefore built from sourced rates but is an upper-bound ESTIMATE: regional premiums are also assessed on property points, and the pension is capped at the same KRW 6,590,000 monthly income ceiling (about KRW 79m a year), neither of which is modelled.
income_tax.local_tax_note: Marginal rates shown already include local income tax of 10% of the tax (PwC, reviewed 2 July 2026). personal_allowance is the basic personal deduction of KRW 1.5 million for the taxpayer (PwC deductions page); the employment income deduction (70% of the first KRW 5m, 40% to KRW 15m, 15% to KRW 45m, 5% to KRW 100m, 2% above; capped at KRW 20m; employees only) and the insurance deductions are not included. Employee contributions: National Pension 4.75% on monthly pay up to KRW 6,590,000 (from July 2026; maximum KRW 313,025 a month), health insurance including long-term care about 4.0674% (monthly cap KRW 10,390,220 in total), employment insurance 0.90%. The pension cap means the 9.7174% total overstates contributions at high pay; no single cap is recorded.

regimes.name: 19% flat tax for foreign employees
regimes.description: Foreign employees who start work in Korea no later than 31 December 2026 may elect a flat 19% rate (excluding 10% local tax, so 20.9%) on employment income instead of progressive 6-45%. Electing forfeits other deductions, exemptions and credits; not available when working for a related-party company. Lasts 20 years from first day of work.
regimes.duration_note: 20 years from the first day of work in Korea through the end of the tax year before the 20-year anniversary. A reform proposal of 3 August 2026 would raise the rate to 21% (23.1% with local tax) and extend the sunset to 31 December 2029 from 1 January 2027; not enacted.

regimes.name: Workation visa (F-1-D)
regimes.description: One-year visa for people who work remotely for a foreign company, with annual income of twice Korea's prior-year GNI per capita (about KRW 85m per the 2024 consulate page), one year of experience in the same industry, age 18+ and KRW 100m medical and repatriation insurance. Local employment is restricted.
